svg.title: QuantMeridian Presidential Impact evidence snapshot
svg.desc: Three analytical findings from the independent public-data reconstruction: the two market constructions closely agree, 24 of 87 annual windows cross a political-control change, and starting CAPE has a modest negative descriptive association with following returns while the starting policy rate does not.

g.text: QuantMeridian PRES — evidence snapshot
Independent public-data reconstruction · descriptive analytics only · no causal or trading claim
Two market constructions agree
correlation of 87 matched annual returns
mean difference: Shiller minus CRSP proxy
The configuration ranking did not change by
return construction on the shared sample.
Political exposure is not fixed
annual windows cross a control change
of the 1936–2022 common sample
A start-date label prevents hindsight relabeling;
it is not a stable full-year policy exposure.
Starting valuation shows a clearer pattern
CAPE-return Pearson r, two constructions
policy-rate-return Pearson r
68 annual windows, 1955–2022; associations
are descriptive and not point-in-time forecasts.
Director implication
Use political labels to structure scenarios; start investment judgment with valuation, expectations, and policy transmission.
QuantMeridian PRES engine outputs from frozen USER_SUPPLIED inputs. CRSP-market proxy and Shiller reconstruction are independent public series, not the seed article’s unrecovered S&P 500 analysis.
